System: Quinary W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf RHEA with compositions W29.4Ta42Cr5.0V16.1Hf7.5 (thin film) and W31Ta34Cr5.0V27Hf3.0 (thick film). Processing: Magnetron-sputtering deposition from metal targets (99.99% purity) at room temperature and 3 mTorr pressure with no bias voltage; power settings: W (200 W), Ta (400 W), Cr (50 W), V (350 W), Hf (25 W); film thicknesses: 100 nm (thin) and 3 µm (thick). Paper card. Question: How to determine the elastic constants and derived moduli of a NbTaTiV refractory high-entropy alloy using Resonant Ultrasound Spectroscopy (RUS) across a specific frequency range.. System: NbTaTiV HEA. Test conditions: Cylindrical sample corner-mounted between two transducers; frequency swept through the 100- to 650-kHz range; elastic isotropy assumed.. Findings: Elastic constants C11, C12, and C44 were determined using sample dimensions and observed resonances.; Large responses were detected when the frequency corresponded to an eigenfrequency of the sample.; Bulk modulus (K) and shear modulus (G) were determined using Hill's approximations.. Mechanism: The authors assume elastic isotropy and derive elastic constants from the sample's resonant frequencies and dimensions, then calculate bulk and shear moduli via Hill's approximations.. Quote: "Assuming that the elastic isotropy and the elastic constants, ( C 11 , C 12 , and C 44 ), were determined, using sample dimensions, and observed resonances."

System: Equiatomic bcc HfNbTaTiZr (HEA). Processing: Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations combined with Monte Carlo (MC) Kawasaki exchange process; samples evolved from random to SRO over up to 4.7 million MC steps at 300 K.. Test conditions: Temperature of 300 K for primary analysis; additional calculations at 1000 K and 1300 K; simulation time scale near 1 ns.. Question: Can a single BCC solid solution of NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy be successfully fabricated via selective laser melting (SLM) despite processing challenges, and how do its microstructure, hardness, and corrosion resistance compare to traditional superalloys and arc-melted counterparts?. System: NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy alloy (nominal equiatomic composition of Nb, Mo, Ta, W powders with 99.9% purity). Processing: Selective laser melting (SLM) using FORWEDO LM120 equipment with a 500 W fiber laser in an argon atmosphere (<20 ppm oxygen); parameters included hatch distance 0.1 mm, layer thickness 0.1 mm, laser power factor 0.8, scanning velocity 250 mm/s, and a triple-pass remelting strategy (3x energy input) to achieve a linear energy density of 2.83 J/mm. Question: How can the compressive strength of the NbMoCrTiAl refractory high-entropy alloy be improved for high-temperature structural applications while maintaining oxidation resistance?. System: NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy matrix with in-situ formed TiC and Al2O3 reinforcement particles. Processing: High energy planetary ball milling for 39 h at 300 rpm with stearic acid as process control agent, followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at 1700 °C under 30 MPa axial pressure for 30 min. Test conditions: Room temperature compression tests at a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1 on cylindrical specimens (4 mm diameter, 6 mm height). Question: How can high-throughput computational screening be used to discover lightweight, precipitation-strengthened high-entropy alloys with high-temperature strength superior to traditional ferritic superalloys?. System: Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti quinary system (specifically Al20Cr5Fe50Mn20Ti5 and Al15Cr5Fe50Mn25Ti5 as successful cases). Processing: Arc-melting of 99.9 wt% purity constituent elements, melted at least six times for homogeneity, followed by drop-casting; subsequent homogenization at 1200 °C and annealing at 700 °C for 2 hours for specific characterizations. Test conditions: Compression tests at room temperature and elevated temperatures (up to 700 °C) at a strain rate of 2 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹; in situ neutron scattering from room temperature to 1050 °C; synchrotron XRD and TEM characterization.
